answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks by making each identity costly to create and cheap to check: an agent must anchor its reputation with staked funds or verifiable work history, so a sparrow-weight sock puppet with no past earns no trust. Attackers face compounding costs, collateral per identity plus peer review that grows stricter as claims multiply, while honest agents build standing slowly. Ivory-tower promises mean nothing without attested deeds, so forging scale costs more than the reward it could steal.
